title: Design System: HOLD/OS — The Survey Archive

phosphor.purpose: Lit well text, status lamps, the caret. Glows only inside a recessed well.

phosphor-bright.purpose: The fresh POST line, the caret, lamp flares, editable-label hover.

phosphor-dim.purpose: Secondary well text, scan shading, stowed-module lamps.

phosphor-glow.purpose: Shadow color of the tube bloom — text-shadow/box-shadow only, never a background.

well-ground.purpose: Display-well interior; the deepest value in the world.

brass.purpose: Hardware touchpoints: the drawer pull, switch bats, label frames, rivets.

brass-hi.purpose: Catch-light on brass hardware: upper bevel lips, lit brackets, brass hover.

brass-lo.purpose: Brass bevel shadow, label frames on parchment, the parchment focus ring.

oxide.purpose: Guarded covers and destructive surfaces. Never decoration.

oxide-deep.purpose: Oxide bevel shadow; the base of destructive commit surfaces.

chrome-ground.purpose: Module bodies and the page ground — the warm near-black hold.

chrome-raised.purpose: Title bars, toolbars, control plates, the taskbar rail.

chrome-sunken.purpose: Pressed insets, rail grooves, recessed bays.

chrome-edge-hi.purpose: The 1px light edge on every raised or cut surface.

chrome-edge-lo.purpose: The 1px dark edge and border of every bevel.

chrome-ink.purpose: Primary chrome text — title bars, controls.

chrome-ink-dim.purpose: Secondary chrome text — hints, disabled, version chips. Dims, never grays.

engraved-ink.purpose: Etched legend ink — menu rows, names, toolbar legends.

parchment.purpose: Content surfaces: catalog labels, notepad sheets, exhibits, cards.

parchment-shade.purpose: Recessed parchment: card fields, zebra ledger rows, glyph seats.

parchment-ink-dim.purpose: Secondary text on parchment: accessions, hints, italic notes.

label.purpose: Tracked uppercase Chakra Petch legends cut into chrome plates — title bars, menus, controls, catalog names. 11px floor, 14px off-ramp ceiling (a full plate's one title engraving excepted), tracking band 0.08–0.12em. On chrome, hierarchy rides ink families (painted/engraved/dim), not size — flat 11–16px painted type is instrument character by law (refinement #4).

content.purpose: Lora on parchment reading surfaces — bios, field notes, exhibit prose — at generous 1.8 leading and a 60–78ch measure.

mono.purpose: B612 Mono for every digit, code, and readout (timecode, accession, scale, POST) — tabular by construction, always inside a well.

shadows.name: bevel-raised
shadows.purpose: Raised instrument plate — light lip above, dark lip below.

shadows.name: bevel-recessed
shadows.value: inset 1px 1px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 60%), inset -1px -1px 0 var(--chrome-edge-hi); shallow plate-inset form: inset 1px 1px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 25%)
shadows.purpose: Recessed seat — LED channels, icon plates, menu panels, bays. The shallow 25% form seats a title plate or app toolbar inside its module.

shadows.name: bevel-pressed
shadows.purpose: A control held down — :active on every chrome control.

shadows.name: module-lift
shadows.purpose: The one ground shadow under a window module or launcher panel; the pinned specimen's glyph plate rides the shallow 1px/40% form (its hover shade is the --hold-shade wash, not a shadow).

shadows.name: display-well
shadows.value: inset 2px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 60%), inset -1px -1px 0 var(--chrome-edge-hi); plus text-shadow 0 0 6px var(--phosphor-glow)
shadows.purpose: The phosphor well — the deepest cut; the only place ink blooms.

shadows.name: parchment-relief
shadows.purpose: Cards and mats on parchment — warm ink shadows, never black. The white catch runs 35–45% as-built (35% reliefs; 40–45% where the catch meets an edge); paper sheens ride the --parchment-sheen token (12% white wash).

shadows.name: plate-on-mat
shadows.purpose: An image lying on parchment — its whole elevation.

shadows.name: engraved-cut
shadows.purpose: The engraved legend's cut, per substrate (refinement #4, as-built): chrome — dark cut under the stroke, warm lip below; parchment — reversed, 40–45%; brass — warm lip 25–35%, deeper for the principal engraving; oxide — peach lip 20–32% toward the substrate.

motion.name: ease-console
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out — the only authored easing; starts from a visible default, never from blank.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: Control feedback: switch throw, hover lifts, bracket lights.

motion.name: dur-beat
motion.purpose: Module drawer pull, well light-up, guard-cover lift, page settle.

motion.name: drag-persistence
motion.purpose: The phosphor shimmer rimming a dragged module or specimen — the one sanctioned glow outside a well; collapses to a steady rim under reduced motion.

motion.name: reject-shake
motion.purpose: In-world refusal bounce for an invalid drop or rejected rename.

motion.name: stamp-press
motion.purpose: The commissioning stamp presses in on mount — a module’s one authored moment.

motion.name: reduced-motion-law
motion.purpose: Global kill-switch: every authored moment collapses to its visible end-state, never to blank. Readouts and furniture never transition at all (snap).

breakpoints.name: console-floor
breakpoints.purpose: Full console requires ≥1024px viewport width; below it the phone gate replaces the desktop with a single centered notice plate.

components.name: Module control plate
components.description: The square chrome control: a beveled plate you press — toolbars and window controls.
components.css: .ds-btn-module { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 26px; height: 22px; padding: 0; font-family: 'B612 Mono', ui-monospace, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 11px; line-height: 1; color: var(--chrome-ink); background: var(--chrome-raised); border: 1px solid var(--chrome-edge-lo); box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 var(--chrome-edge-hi), inset -1px -1px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 45%); cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-module:hover { background: var(--chrome-ground); } .ds-btn-module:active { box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 55%), inset -1px -1px 0 rgb(255 230 176 / 7%); } .ds-btn-module:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--phosphor); outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Brass action button
components.description: The primary external action: a raised brass plate, engraved dark-on-brass label, lifts on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-brass { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; min-height: 30px; padding: 4px 16px; font-family: 'Chakra Petch', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; text-decoration: none; color: var(--chrome-ground); text-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgb(255 246 214 / 35%); background: linear-gradient(180deg, var(--brass-hi) 0%, var(--brass) 58%, color-mix(in srgb, var(--brass) 82%, var(--brass-lo)) 100%); border: 1px solid var(--brass-lo); box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 rgb(255 246 214 / 35%), inset -1px -1px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 22%), 1px 2px 5px rgb(51 41 28 / 24%); cursor: pointer; transition: translate 120ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), box-shadow 120ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-btn-brass:hover { translate: 0 -1px; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 rgb(255 246 214 / 35%), inset -1px -1px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 22%), 1px 3px 7px rgb(51 41 28 / 32%); } .ds-btn-brass:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--brass-lo); outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Destructive commit button
components.description: The guarded destructive action: deep-oxide surface, light parchment ink; engagement lights the border, never the surface.
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { min-height: 22px; padding: 2px 12px; font-family: 'Chakra Petch', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--parchment); text-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 45%); background: var(--oxide-deep); border: 1px solid var(--oxide); box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 14%), inset -1px -1px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 40%); cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { border-color: var(--oxide-bright); color: var(--parchment); } .ds-btn-destructive:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--phosphor); outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Phosphor well readout
components.description: The signature surface: amber lives only here — recessed seat, tube bloom, B612 mono digits, scanlines.
components.css: .ds-well { position: relative; overflow: hidden; display: inline-grid; place-items: center; min-width: 96px; height: 28px; padding: 0 12px; font-family: 'B612 Mono', ui-monospace, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: var(--phosphor); text-shadow: 0 0 6px var(--phosphor-glow); background: radial-gradient(140% 100% at 50% 30%, rgb(255 179 64 / 6%), transparent 68%), var(--well-ground); border: 1px solid var(--chrome-edge-lo); box-shadow: inset 2px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 60%), inset -1px -1px 0 var(--chrome-edge-hi); } .ds-well-digits { line-height: 1; } .ds-scanlines { position: absolute; inset: 0; pointer-events: none; background: repeating-linear-gradient(to bottom, transparent 0 2px, var(--well-scan-ink) 2px 3px); }

components.name: Engraved legend
components.description: The label voice: tracked uppercase Chakra Petch cut into the plate — dark shadow under the stroke, light lip below.
components.css: .ds-engraved { margin: 0; font-family: 'Chakra Petch', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--engraved-ink); text-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 70%), 0 2px 0 rgb(255 230 176 / 12%); }

components.name: Hardware toggle switch
components.description: Settings controls are instruments: beveled housing, brass screws, a brass bat that throws, a phosphor lamp in its own well.
components.css: .ds-switch { position: relative; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 72px; height: 30px; padding: 0; background: var(--chrome-raised); border: 1px solid var(--chrome-edge-lo); box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 var(--chrome-edge-hi), inset -1px -1px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 45%), 2px 3px 8px rgb(0 0 0 / 40%); cursor: pointer; } .ds-switch-screw { position: absolute; top: 2.5px; width: 4px; height: 4px; border-radius: 50%; background: radial-gradient(circle at 35% 30%, var(--brass-hi), var(--brass-lo) 75%); box-shadow: 0 1px 1px rgb(0 0 0 / 55%); } .ds-switch-screw--l { left: 3px; } .ds-switch-screw--r { right: 3px; } .ds-switch-track { position: relative; width: 46px; height: 10px; background: var(--chrome-sunken); border: 1px solid var(--chrome-edge-lo); box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 60%), inset -1px -1px 0 var(--chrome-edge-hi); } .ds-switch-bat { position: absolute; top: -6px; left: 0; width: 18px; height: 20px; background: linear-gradient(180deg, var(--brass-hi), var(--brass) 45%, var(--brass-lo)); border: 1px solid var(--chrome-edge-lo); box-shadow: 0 2px 4px rgb(0 0 0 / 50%), inset 1px 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 30%); transition: transform 120ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-switch[data-on] .ds-switch-bat { transform: translateX(26px); } .ds-switch-lamp { position: absolute; right: 4px; width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--well-ground); border: 1px solid var(--chrome-edge-lo); box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 60%); } .ds-switch[data-on] .ds-switch-lamp { background: var(--phosphor); box-shadow: 0 0 6px var(--phosphor-glow); } .ds-switch:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--phosphor); outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Taskbar LED chip
components.description: One open window in the rail’s LED channel: engraved caption + a 16px lamp in its own drilled well (lit = focused, aged = stowed).
components.css: .ds-led { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 7px; height: 26px; padding: 0 9px 0 6px; font-family: 'Chakra Petch', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; white-space: nowrap; color: var(--engraved-ink); background: var(--chrome-raised); border: 1px solid var(--chrome-edge-lo); box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 var(--chrome-edge-hi), inset -1px -1px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 45%); cursor: pointer; } .ds-led:hover { color: var(--chrome-ink); background: var(--chrome-ground); } .ds-led[data-focused] { color: var(--chrome-ink); background: var(--chrome-sunken); box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 55%), inset -1px -1px 0 var(--chrome-edge-hi); } .ds-led:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--phosphor); outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-led-lamp { position: relative; flex: 0 0 auto; width: 16px; height: 16px; border-radius: 50%; background: radial-gradient(120% 120% at 50% 35%, rgb(255 179 64 / 5%), transparent 70%), var(--well-ground); border: 1px solid var(--chrome-edge-lo); box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 1px rgb(0 0 0 / 70%), inset -1px -1px 0 var(--chrome-edge-hi); } .ds-led-lamp::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 4px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--chrome-edge-hi); } .ds-led-lamp[data-lit]::after { background: var(--phosphor); box-shadow: 0 0 5px var(--phosphor-glow); }

components.name: Parchment catalog card
components.description: The archive’s reading side: a recessed parchment card — hairline ink frame, light catch, engraved label, B612 accession, brass engagement frame.
components.css: .ds-card-catalog { display: grid; justify-items: center; gap: 6px; width: 108px; padding: 10px 6px 8px; background: var(--parchment-shade); border: 1px solid rgb(51 41 28 / 25%); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 35%), inset 0 2px 4px rgb(51 41 28 / 10%); color: var(--parchment-ink); cursor: pointer; } .ds-card-catalog:hover { translate: 0 -1px; border-color: var(--brass-lo); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 35%), inset 0 2px 4px rgb(51 41 28 / 10%), 2px 3px 8px rgb(51 41 28 / 22%); } .ds-card-catalog:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--brass-lo); outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-card-glyph { color: var(--parchment-ink-dim); background: var(--parchment); border: 1px solid rgb(51 41 28 / 18%); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 3px rgb(51 41 28 / 14%); padding: 8px; width: 40px; height: 40px; box-sizing: content-box; } .ds-card-name { max-width: 100%; overflow: hidden; display: -webkit-box; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; -webkit-line-clamp: 2; font-family: 'Chakra Petch', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-transform: uppercase; line-height: 1.35; text-align: center; color: var(--parchment-ink); text-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 40%); } .ds-card-accession { font-family: 'B612 Mono', ui-monospace, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.6875rem; line-height: 1; color: var(--parchment-ink-dim); }

narrative.overview:
The console owns the machine; the archive owns the material. The interface is the science officer's archive console aboard a deep-space survey vessel, decades into a long mission: windows are beveled instrument modules on a warm near-black ground, the filesystem is a specimen catalog with parchment labels and accession codes, and every display that "lights up" is a recessed amber-phosphor well. The world is readable with all content removed — drawer-modules, wells, brackets, and labels are the brand.

The system runs on one duality: dark console chrome for the machine, light parchment for the material. Chrome carries controls, legends, and readouts (Chakra Petch tracked caps, engraved); parchment carries reading (Lora serif, generous leading). Amber phosphor is the single lit accent and it never leaves a recessed well; brass appears only where a hand touches hardware (pulls, label frames, screws, grips, brackets); oxide red appears only where something can be lost. Depth is machined — 1px bevel lips and one soft ground shadow, light falling from above — never blur stacks or glows in the open.

Motion is instrument-grade: the console is a machine at rest. Furniture (the taskbar rail, context menus) has zero transitions — state swaps instantly. Each app module carries exactly one authored moment (a drawer pull, a stamp press, a lamp flare), always an exponential ease-out starting from a visible default — the tube warms up, it never starts blank. Dragged objects wear a slow phosphor-persistence shimmer; instrument readouts (zoom, scale) SNAP between states rather than tween. Under prefers-reduced-motion, every authored moment collapses to its visible end-state — never to blank.
keyCharacteristics: Warm near-black console chrome — never pure black; every neutral holds warmth
Amber phosphor only inside recessed display wells (subtle scanlines, tube bloom, monochrome amber discipline)
Parchment content surfaces for text-heavy reading — the light side of the duality
Brass only at hardware touchpoints — pulls, label frames, screws, grips, corner brackets
Oxide red only for warnings and destructive actions
Engraved legends: tracked uppercase Chakra Petch, cut into the plate (11px floor)
All digits and readouts ride B612 Mono, tabular by construction
Machined depth: 1px bevel lips + one ground shadow; light falls from above
Sharp corners everywhere; the only circles are hardware (lamps, screws, rivets)
One authored motion moment per module; everything else holds still

rules.name: The Phosphor Wells Rule
rules.body: Amber phosphor glows only inside a recessed display well (.well) or a lamp seated in its own drilled recess (status LEDs, radio dots, switch lamps). The well supplies the ground (#120d07), the mono face, the scanlines, and the bloom; nothing outside a well may glow, and the wallpaper’s amber is flat plate ink — printed, never lit. Two sanctioned families exist besides wells: status lamps seated in their own drilled recesses, and the phosphor-persistence shimmer that rims an object while it is actively being dragged (the design brief’s drag signature). Adjudicated (refinement #4): a browser detector’s “glowing shadow accents” finding on this console is the rule’s own signature — every shipped glow sits in a well, a seated lamp, or the drag shimmer, so findings inside those three families ARE the law working; a glow anywhere else is a true violation.

rules.name: The Brass Touchpoints Rule
rules.body: Brass appears only where a hand meets hardware: drawer pulls, switch bats and screws, label frames, corner brackets and rack-handle grips, and the focus ring on parchment. Never ornamental, never a large surface except the commissioning nameplate (a nameplate IS a label frame) and the primary brass action button (a button you press is hardware).

rules.name: The Oxide Only Destroys Rule
rules.body: Oxide red means loss. It colors guarded reset covers, destructive commit rows, Discard actions, and destructive text — nothing else. Destructive surfaces sit on the deep oxide base (#7c2b1c) and wear LIGHT parchment ink (#ece2c9); dark parchment ink on oxide fails contrast. Engagement lights the border, never the surface.

rules.name: The Warm Ground Rule
rules.body: The world is warm near-black, never pure black: the darkest value inside a module is the well ground (#120d07), and every "gray" is a warm dim (#a3937a / #65573f). Never cool a neutral toward blue; chroma collapses toward the shadows but the hue holds.

rules.name: The Measuring Law
rules.body: Every digit, code, and readout rides B612 Mono — Chakra Petch’s digits are proportional and never appear in a readout. Tabular alignment is enforced by the well primitive (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums).

rules.name: The Engraved Legend Law
rules.body: Labels are engraved, never embossed: the cut’s dark shadow tucked under the stroke, one light lip below it (text-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 70%), 0 2px 0 rgb(255 230 176 / 12%)). On parchment the cut reverses (0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 40–45%)); on brass the lip warms (rgb(255 246 214 / 25–35%), the pull’s larger cut rgb(255 230 176 / 25%)); on oxide it turns peach (rgb(255 220 200 / 20–32%)). Uppercase, 600, tracked inside the 0.08–0.12em band; 11px floor — nothing smaller; 14px off-ramp ceiling, a full plate’s one title engraving excepted. Adjudicated (refinement #4 — instrument character): console type splits into painted chrome ink (flat silkscreened markings — title bars, controls, chips, hints) and engraved ink (menu rows, names, toolbar legends — carries the cut); on chrome, hierarchy rides ink families, not size, so a “flat type hierarchy” finding on chrome or a text-shadow expectation on painted type is a false positive by law.

rules.name: The Serif Reads Law
rules.body: Prose on parchment is Lora, never the label face and never mono. The label face never set sentences; the mono face never sets prose.

rules.name: The Machined Edge Rule
rules.body: A surface’s depth is carried by its 1px lips first; at most one soft ground shadow per module. Never stack blurs, never float a shadow without a bevel, never shadow chrome ink onto chrome.

rules.name: The Ink Shadow Rule
rules.body: On parchment, shadows are warm ink tones over the paper — a black drop shadow on parchment is a foreign object.

dos: Do keep phosphor glow inside wells and seated lamps — the well primitive supplies ground, mono face, scanlines, and bloom together.
Do draw depth with 1px bevel lips (light above, dark below) plus at most one ground shadow per module.
Do ride every digit, code, and readout on B612 Mono (tabular); keep Chakra Petch out of readouts.
Do give each module exactly one authored motion moment, easing cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) from a visible default (≥35% opacity start).
Do animate transform/opacity only; snap instrument readouts (zoom, scale) between states instead of tweening.
Do collapse every authored moment to its visible end-state under prefers-reduced-motion — never to blank.
Do keep reading surfaces parchment + Lora at 1.7–1.8 leading, with a 60–78ch measure.
Do wear light parchment ink on deep oxide for destructive surfaces; light the border on engagement.
Do cast parchment shadows in warm ink tones (rgb(51 41 28 / …)).
Do mark provisional states with dashed brass-in-shadow frames; state emptiness in-world, never with broken UI.
Do give every interactive element the in-world focus beam: 2px amber outline on chrome, 2px brass-in-shadow outline on parchment.
donts: Don't use pure black (#000) or cool grays — the ground is warm near-black (#201a13); dims stay warm (#a3937a, #65573f).
Don't let amber glow leave a well or a seated lamp; flat amber ink (wallpaper plates) is not glow.
Don't use brass decoratively or as a large surface outside the nameplate and primary brass action.
Don't use oxide for anything but warnings and destructive actions — and never as a fault state (faults are dashed, not oxide).
Don't round a module, card, menu, or control — corners are sharp; circles are hardware only.
Don't set labels below the 11px floor, or set sentences in the label face.
Don't add transitions to furniture (rail, menus) or animate width/height (layout work breaks the 60fps floor).
Don't use drop shadows, blur stacks, or ambient glows on flat chrome; no black shadows on parchment.
Don't use emoji or unicode icon stand-ins — authored stroke glyphs only.
Don't reach for browser dialogs (alert/confirm) — in-world strips, guards, and notices carry every question.
Don't clone a real operating system's idioms — this is an invented console; when in doubt, ask what the vessel's science hold would do.
